_doc: The metronome's phase table (OPS_METRONOME_PROVE_IN_SHADOW, OPS_METRONOME_MIGRATE_CLOCKS_FENCED; design/RimMandrake/operations_metronome_strategy_2026-11-02.md §2, §8 step 5). Read by src/RimMandrake/Utils/metronome.py, validated by `metronome.py lint`. Phases run in the order sense, remember, raise, ring, dispatch, chores; a phase is due when beat % every == offset, when it is overdue, or when one of its wall-clock slots is due. budget_s bounds the whole beat; raise and ring (and any overdue phase) are reserved first. A phase without owns is in shadow: its command only reads or writes inside {state} (ops_watch's own store there, the Dispatcher's dry tick). A phase with owns has replaced those old timers (disabled at cutover, one clock a day) and runs its real command carrying {gen}, its ownership generation (metronome.may_act). raise owns rm-restart-reconcile.timer since 2026-11-04: 500 of 500 shadow passes exited 0, max 1.2 s; the real pass reads transcripts and may file in process: 12 s at cutover, 8 s since 2026-11-05 (1247 real passes, max 2.0 s), so the reserve (raise and ring with cleanup, 18 s) leaves sense and remember their 27 s and an overdue remember no longer defers sense every other beat. sense owns rm-ops-watch.timer since 2026-11-05 (its real store /mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/ops_watch, --file-alarms; 10:05-13:35Z shadow: 7 of 170 pairs overran 15 s, each family still read every ~13 min against the old timer's 15), dispatch owns rm-dispatcher.timer since 2026-11-06 (tick --apply, fenced by {gen}, bounded to the beat deadline), and remember writes the real memory (ops_memory build, no --wait-ingest: the next beat's build sees what VM had not yet ingested); the old unit's nightly red reruns run as rm-ops-reds.timer. limit_s values are ESTIMATES (ops_watch: 73 s for all 20 families, so 2 per beat); measure them from beats.jsonl before cutover (step 6); first shadow beats, 2026-11-04: steve+testing 1.5 s, but accounts+codex and disk+timers each overran 15 s, so per-family timing decides the pairing before cutover. chores has no shadow command yet: its four timers stay the owners. sense runs ops_watch --compose since 2026-11-05 (every family not measured this beat carried from its series with observed_at, alarms and the health verdict made on the beat that measures flow, which joins testing for its ctx, so testing sits between flow and the light production), fenced by {gen}; its codex and queues reads are cached (24 s and 16 s alone before, ~4 s and ~3 s warm).

sense.reason: limit 15 kept: 161 of 1269 beats overran it (median 7.0 s, p95 15.1, max 17.6), so shortening only adds overruns; consumer: ops_watch store, remember reads it, ops_clocks owns rm-ops-watch.timer.

remember.reason: limit 8 kept: median 0.6 s, p95 1.5, max 8.1; its 51 overruns are budget-squeezed beats, not slow runs; consumer: ops_memory store.

raise.reason: limit 8 to 4 (2026-11-06): 1275 passes, max 1.9 s, p95 0.66; owns rm-restart-reconcile.timer. The freed reserve goes to sense and remember.

ring.reason: limit 6 to 2 (2026-11-06): 1276 passes, max 0.68 s, p95 0.17; dispatcher status, critical max_ok_age_s read by the sense deadman.

dispatch.reason: limit 20 kept: shadow dry ticks median 2.4 s, p95 7.5, max 14.8 over 606 passes (24 h to 2026-11-06); real --apply ticks ran p95 21 s, max 97 s under the old timer, so the tick stops starting acts 6 s before METRONOME_DEADLINE and gives the rest back (dispatcher.py, eb7ac0db13). Owns rm-dispatcher.timer since 2026-11-06; every 2 beats (~140 s) against the old timer's 120 s.

chores.reason: no command: costs 0.0 s per beat (256 no_command lines, no budget used); kept only because metronome.ORDER and the slot selftests require the name; the four old timers still own the chores.
chores.why_no_command: scratch pressure, account plan and usage keep their own timers until cutover
